abstract: Extracellular ATP and adenosine operate as tightly coupled purinergic signals, yet tracking both molecules simultaneously in vivo has been limited by the performance and spectral range of existing sensors. We describe an expanded set of genetically encoded GPCR-Activation-Based (GRAB) sensors for ATP and adenosine that together support multiplexed imaging of purinergic signaling in the intact brain. Systematic optimization of receptor scaffolds, membrane trafficking, and fluorophore coupling yielded next-generation green sensors (Ado2h, Ado2m, ATP2h, ATP2l) and spectrally separated red variants (rAdo1h, rATP1h), each combining high ligand specificity, genetically targetable expression, sub-second kinetics, and minimal engagement of endogenous GPCR pathways. This combination allows minimally invasive, dual-color imaging of purinergic activity in vivo. Using multiplexed fiber photometry and two-photon imaging, we tracked ATP and adenosine concurrently across several behavioral and pathological settings. ATP release preceded extracellular adenosine accumulation during sleep-wake transitions and neuronal activation, a pattern consistent with extracellular ATP hydrolysis as a substantial contributor to in vivo adenosine signaling. During epileptic seizures, paired imaging of extracellular ATP with extracellular adenosine, and of extracellular with intracellular adenosine, indicated distinct spatiotemporal dynamics across cellular compartments. This expanded sensor set offers a platform for multiplexed purinergic imaging and for probing ATP-adenosine coupling across physiological and pathological brain states.
